story.title: Russian Missiles Land in Poland Amid NATO Exercises
story.summary: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in Poland, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk described as likely an intentional provocation. This incident coincided with European military exercises in Poland related to a potential postwar mission in Ukraine. NATO has labeled the missile landings a 'grave violation' of Polish airspace.

timeline_highlights.title: Zelenskyy Seeks Path to Putin Meeting Through Abu Dhabi Talks
timeline_highlights.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope that upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi could pave the way for a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. During a meeting in Berlin with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, both leaders emphasized the importance of including the EU in peace negotiations with Russia. Merz voiced skepticism regarding Russia's commitment to a truce.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine War
event_overview.subject: Ukraine War
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine War is the interstate conflict centered on Russia’s use of armed force against Ukraine, with roots in Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine and a full-scale Russian invasion launched on February 24, 2022. It combines active military operations, diplomacy over a possible settlement, international assistance and sanctions, displacement, and investigations into alleged international crimes.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: The broader conflict dates to 2014; the International Court of Justice’s March 16, 2022 order identifies the Russian military operations at issue as having commenced in Ukraine on February 24, 2022.

facts.label: Parties and geography
facts.value: The war principally concerns Ukraine and the Russian Federation and is fought on Ukrainian territory; Belarus has also been cited by the European Union for involvement in Russia’s 2022 invasion.

facts.label: International legal framework
facts.value: The UN Charter requires members to refrain from the threat or use of force against another state’s territorial integrity or political independence. The UN General Assembly adopted resolution ES-11/1 on March 2, 2022, titled “Aggression against Ukraine,” by a vote of 141–5 with 35 abstentions.

facts.label: International court proceedings
facts.value: In provisional measures issued March 16, 2022, the ICJ ordered Russia to suspend the military operations it had commenced on February 24, 2022; the order was made in Ukraine’s case under the Genocide Convention and did not resolve the merits of the dispute.

facts.label: Accountability process
facts.value: The International Criminal Court opened its Ukraine investigation on March 2, 2022. Its stated scope covers alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity, or genocide committed by any person on any part of Ukraine’s territory since November 21, 2013.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows selected diplomacy and security developments connected to the war, including proposed leader-level contacts and regional military incidents; it does not aim to provide a complete record of battlefield operations, negotiations, sanctions, humanitarian impacts, or legal proceedings.

related_stories.title: Zelenskyy Labels Putin a 'Killer' Following Deadly Russian Strikes in Kyiv
related_stories.summary: Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a 'killer' after a major wave of Russian strikes targeted Kyiv, resulting in at least seven fatalities. The attacks involved over 400 drones and 110 missiles, causing significant damage to infrastructure, including key bridges across the Dnipro River.

related_stories.summary: On November 20, 2026, an autonomous electric flying taxi successfully completed a passenger flight during a demonstration in Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. The pilotless aircraft, built in China, took off vertically and flew autonomously, showcasing potential advancements in urban transportation.

related_stories.title: International Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
related_stories.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has made a historic ruling, declaring Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority during a military campaign in 2017. This unprecedented decision, which found intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population, marks the first time a state has been held accountable for genocide by the ICJ. The ruling has sparked varied international reactions, with Myanmar rejecting it as 'unfair' and calls for sanctions against the country emerging from rights groups. The ICJ's decision may also influence future cases regarding genocide, including allegations against Israel.

related_stories.title: Russian Strike on Kyiv Results in Eight Deaths and Extensive Damage
related_stories.summary: A Russian attack on Kyiv on November 20, 2026, resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and left many injured. The assault was described by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as one of the largest of the war. Emergency crews are currently searching through the wreckage, battling fires, and assessing damage to buildings and warehouses across the capital.
